project.name: Monoid-algebra units, augmentation, Laurent coordinates and finite-abelian Fourier convolution
project.description: Reusable Lean algebra equivalences from group algebras equipped with explicit free-abelian coordinates to multivariable Laurent polynomial algebras, with canonical FreeAbelianGroup specialization and forward/inverse basis and free-generator laws. Laurent monomials are finitely supported integer exponent vectors; no finite-variable or decidable-equality premise is added. Separately, field-valued finite-abelian characters give evaluation bases when enough roots exist; right convolution has positive-character eigenvalues, diagonalization and a Nat.card rank formula. Monoid-algebra augmentation sums coefficients over any semiring and monoid. For a right-cancellative monoid M, any nonzero R[M]-linear map from R with its left augmentation action into the left regular R[M] forces M finite. Such maps vanish for infinite M, including infinite groups, without coefficient commutativity, nontriviality or a domain condition. Over any ring, the augmentation kernel is the left ideal generated by single m 1 - 1. A monoid generating set, or a subgroup generating set for groups, suffices for these left-ideal generators. Generic difference-membership lemmas propagate through monoid and subgroup closure in any ring's left ideals. As a left coefficient-ring module it also has a basis indexed by nonidentity monoid elements, with those vectors and the original coefficients as coordinates. A generic pointed Finsupp sum-kernel equivalence underlies this basis. Single-term units over nontrivial semirings are exactly the terms whose coefficient and monoid index are both units. Coefficient-unit reflection holds over every semiring, including the trivial one. For an arbitrary subgroup of a group, its left ideal of basis differences consists of exactly the elements with zero coefficient sums on left cosets. Over a nontrivial ring these ideals reflect subgroup membership and inclusion, and two-sidedness is equivalent to subgroup normality. No group or coefficient commutativity or finiteness is needed. The coset map itself is semiring-general. Subgroup finite generation implies finite generation of its left group-ring ideal over any ring; over a nontrivial ring the converse holds. For the whole group this characterizes finite generation of the augmentation kernel. Left-Noetherian group algebras over nontrivial rings have every subgroup finitely generated. Surjective augmentation combines with the generic surjective-homomorphism Noetherianity theorem for coefficient descent over arbitrary semirings and monoids. For a finitely generated commutative monoid, its monoid algebra over any left-Noetherian ring is left-Noetherian, in independent universes and without coefficient commutativity. Augmentation gives the reverse implication; the exponent monoid need not be finite. For any monoid homomorphism over any ring, its monoid-algebra kernel is the left ideal spanned by all equal-image unit-basis differences. A finitely generated commutative source admits one finite pair family that works over every coefficient ring, without coefficient Noetherianity or target commutativity, finite generation or surjectivity. More generally, finite generation of the integer kernel is an explicit sufficient premise. For any injective homomorphism from a group to a monoid, left-Noetherianity of the monoid algebra descends to the group algebra over every semiring, with three independent universes. Every subgroup algebra is therefore left-Noetherian, without finite index or normality. The generic criterion uses an additive right retraction and ideal extension-contraction; no target cancellation or freeness is assumed. For any semiring and subgroup, right cosets index a basis of the group algebra as a left subgroup-algebra module, with explicit coefficient, reconstruction and scalar compatibility laws. Finite index makes this module finite over any semiring. For ring coefficients, finite-index subgroup algebras and group algebras are left-Noetherian simultaneously. Over every ring, the infinite cyclic group algebra is left-Noetherian iff its coefficient ring is. Group equivalences and finite-index infinite cyclic subgroups transport this criterion, including finite-group products. Every left ideal of an arbitrary semiring extends along monoid-algebra constants to exactly the elements whose coefficients lie in that ideal. Coefficient-change kernels are therefore extended coefficient kernels. Their powers vanish at exactly the same exponents as the coefficient kernel, including degree zero, for arbitrary semiring homomorphisms and monoids. With ring source and semiring target coefficients, surjectivity identifies the quotient with the target monoid algebra; otherwise it is the range subsemiring. Polynomial transport preserves constants, every coefficient, ideal extension and coefficient-change kernels. For a group-to-monoid map, simultaneous coefficient/index change over a ring source has kernel the sum of the subgroup-relation ideal and the extended coefficient kernel. Surjective coefficients give the algebra of the index range; if the index map is also surjective the full target is available. No nontriviality or commutativity is imposed, and the target coefficients need only be a semiring. No sufficient-condition converse for arbitrary groups is asserted. Over a nontrivial possibly noncommutative ring with prime p equal to zero, nilpotence of the augmentation kernel implies one common p-power exponent for an arbitrary group, hence IsPGroup p G, without finiteness. Uniform vanishing of mixed ordered products gives the same conclusion. A generic left-ideal power API over any semiring identifies zero powers with vanishing of every ordered product of that length, including degree zero. For finite p-groups over any ring with p=0, including the zero ring, the augmentation kernel has zero Nat.card G-th power. Every ordered mixed product of that length therefore vanishes. Over nontrivial rings, finite-group augmentation nilpotence is equivalent to IsPGroup p G. The proof uses central subgroups of order p, canonical cyclic quotient kernels, ideal extension bounds and multiplication of power degrees. For locally finite p-groups over any ring with prime p=0, each augmentation-zero element is nilpotent, with an element-dependent exponent. Under these same hypotheses, the Jacobson radical is the augmentation preimage of the coefficient radical. Radical membership is detected by augmentation, and a basis term is radical exactly when its coefficient is. If the coefficient radical is zero, the group-algebra radical equals the augmentation kernel. No uniform kernel exponent or vanishing kernel power is asserted; noncommutative and zero coefficient rings are allowed. Uniform nilpotence of an ordinary left-ideal action over any semiring yields a nonzero common annihilated vector in every nontrivial semimodule. Two-sided ideals have a canonical common-annihilator submodule, agreeing with commutative set torsion. For any ring and monoid, augmentation-kernel annihilation is equivalent to being fixed by every canonical monoid symbol. Every nontrivial unital module of a finite p-group algebra over a ring with prime p=0 therefore has a nonzero canonical fixed vector, without finite generation, finite dimension or finiteness of the module. Simple modules of these finite p-group algebras have trivial group action on every vector, hence augmentation action. Simplicity over the group algebra is equivalent to simplicity under canonical restriction along singleOneRingHom, including noncommutative and zero coefficient rings. The augmentation-action/trivial-monoid-action characterization is valid for semirings and semimodules. For any map of modules over a finite p-group algebra with prime p=0 in any ring, canonical fixed vectors detect injectivity and canonical augmentation coinvariants detect surjectivity, without finite generation or coupled module universes. The generic injection theorem concerns nilpotent two-sided ideals over semirings acting on additive groups; quotient surjectivity detection allows nilpotent left ideals over rings. Nilpotent Nakayama itself holds for arbitrary semimodules. For arbitrary rings S and A, any ring homomorphism phi, a given A-module V, and a two-sided ideal I with one power contained in the annihilator of V, surjectivity of the canonical S-to-A/I map implies separate Noetherian and Artinian equivalences and equality of composition lengths in ENat under exact restriction along phi. This includes nilpotent ideals, infinite length, noncentral scalar images and zero rings, without finite generation. For any ring R with prime p=0 and finite p-group G, these three invariants of every given R[G]-module agree with canonical coefficient restriction. For a finite group whose order is a unit in any semiring, projectivity under canonical coefficient restriction implies projectivity of the original group-algebra module. Noncommutative and zero semirings, additive commutative monoids and independent coefficient, group and module universes are allowed. Monoid algebras commute canonically with finite square matrix semirings, preserving every coefficient entry. The equivalence requires a semiring, a monoid and a finite decidable matrix index type in independent universes; empty indices and zero or noncommutative coefficients are allowed. Group-algebra centrality over any semiring is equivalent to central coefficients and conjugation invariance. A nonzero coefficient of a central element has a finite conjugation orbit, even when the group is infinite. At any one fixed group index, coefficients of all right products determine a group-algebra element; left-product tests independently do so. Either family detects zero, over any possibly zero or noncommutative semiring and any group, without finiteness. Identity evaluation is the index-one case, not augmentation. No group-algebra/convolution bridge is asserted.

headlines.text:
The families below summarize the library. The
[complete catalogue](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md) retains the detailed statements,
qualifiers and source links; the [usage guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/Usage.md) provides the
module and declaration inventories.

headlines.title: Single terms and augmentation
headlines.text:
**Single terms and augmentation.** Over a nontrivial semiring and any monoid,
`IsUnit (single m r) ↔ IsUnit r ∧ IsUnit m`; coefficient-unit reflection
also allows the zero semiring. Over any semiring and an index type with
only multiplication, a single term is left-regular iff its coefficient is
left-regular and either the coefficients are subsingleton or its index is
left-regular; the [right-hand criterion](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/GroupRings/MonoidAlgebra/Regular.lean)
is analogous. Augmentation is the coefficient-sum ring
homomorphism over any semiring. For a right-cancellative monoid `M`, a nonzero
`R[M]`-linear map from `R` with its left augmentation action into the left
regular `R[M]` forces `M` finite; all such maps vanish when `M` is infinite,
including infinite groups. No coefficient nontriviality or domain condition
is needed. See the [augmentation Hom theorems](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/GroupRings/MonoidAlgebra/AugmentationHom.lean).
Over a ring its kernel is the **left** span of `single m 1 - 1`, with monoid
or subgroup generating-set refinements.
`MonoidAlgebra.augmentationKerBasis` is a basis over the coefficient ring
`R`, **not** over `R[M]`, indexed by nonidentity monoid elements.
[Statements and modules](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#single-terms-and-augmentation).
Over a nontrivial semiring and any group `G`, projectivity of `R` over
`R[G]` for the canonical **left augmentation action** forces `G` to be
finite and `(Nat.card G : R)` to be a unit; coefficients need not commute.
See the [augmentation-projectivity theorem](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/GroupRings/MonoidAlgebra/AugmentationProjective.lean).

headlines.title: Units with two unique products
headlines.text:
**Units with two unique products.** Over a no-zero-divisor semiring `R`
and a monoid `M` with `TwoUniqueProds M`, an arbitrary `f : R[M]` is a unit
iff `f = single m.val r.val` for some `m : Units M` and `r : Units R`.
Both kinds of units are multiplicative; `R` may be the zero semiring.
For an additive monoid `A` with `TwoUniqueSums A`, the companion theorem
uses `a : AddUnits A`; coefficient and algebra units remain multiplicative.
See the [unit theorem](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/GroupRings/MonoidAlgebra/UnitsUniqueProds.lean) and
[precise scope and zero-semiring boundary](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#units-with-two-unique-products).

headlines.title: Convolution support
headlines.text:
**Convolution support.** Over a no-zero-divisor semiring and a magma with
two unique products, a product of input support cardinalities greater than
one forces the convolution support cardinality to be greater than one.
Coefficients need not commute, and no monoid or nontriviality assumption is
imposed. See
[`MonoidAlgebra.one_lt_card_support_coeff_mul`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/GroupRings/MonoidAlgebra/SupportUniqueProds.lean)
and the [precise support bound](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#convolution-support).

headlines.title: Coefficient tests, centers and finite matrices
headlines.text:
**Coefficient tests, centers and finite matrices.** Over any possibly zero
or noncommutative semiring, a group-algebra element is determined by one
chosen coefficient after all right multiplications, and independently after
all left multiplications. Centrality means central coefficients invariant
under conjugation; coefficients vanish on infinite conjugacy orbits.
For any monoid, finite decidable matrix indices give the ring equivalence
`MonoidAlgebra (Matrix n n R) M ≃+* Matrix n n (R[M])`, preserving both
multiplication orders, including empty indices.
[Precise statements](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#coefficient-tests-and-finite-matrices).

headlines.title: Crossed maps and averaging
headlines.text:
**Crossed maps and averaging.** Over any ring and monoid, linear maps from
the full augmentation ideal to a given left `R[M]`-module correspond
additively to normalized crossed maps
`z(mn) = z(m) + single m 1 • z(n)` for its canonical action.
For a finite group of unit order in the coefficient ring, every crossed map
is principal, with negative inverse-order sum witness, natural for additive
maps. See the [universal property](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/GroupRings/MonoidAlgebra/AugmentationCrossedUniversal.lean)
and [averaging](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/GroupRings/MonoidAlgebra/AugmentationAveraging.lean).

headlines.title: Augmentation cotangents
headlines.text:
**Augmentation cotangents.** For any unital ring and monoid, coefficient-linear
maps from `I/I²` to a left `R`-module `V` correspond **as a set** to
`M →* Multiplicative V`. For a group,
`I/I² ≃ₗ[R] R ⊗[ℤ] Additive (Abelianization G)`, where `I` is the augmentation
ideal and `I²` its ordinary ideal square. Coefficient covariance is semilinear; monoid products split by projections
and sums of inclusions. No commutativity or freeness is required.
[Statements](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#augmentation-cotangents) ·
[cotangent guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/AugmentationCotangent.md).

headlines.title: Finite `p`-groups and fixed vectors
headlines.text:
**Finite `p`-groups and fixed vectors.** For prime `p`, any ring with
`(p : R) = 0` and finite `p`-group `G`, the augmentation ideal has zero
`Nat.card G`-th power. Every nontrivial unital `R[G]`-module has a nonzero
canonical fixed vector; simplicity is equivalent to simplicity under
canonical coefficient restriction, and simple modules have trivial group
action. For any group over any ring, augmentation nilpotence forces
`Subsingleton R ∨ Finite G`, without a characteristic assumption. If
`(p : R) = 0`, nilpotence is equivalent to
`Subsingleton R ∨ (Finite G ∧ IsPGroup p G)`; over nontrivial `R` it also
forces one common `p`-power exponent. For locally finite `p`-groups over
any ring with `(p : R) = 0`, every augmentation-zero element is nilpotent,
with an element-dependent exponent; no uniform kernel power is asserted.
Under these same locally finite hypotheses, the Jacobson radical is the
augmentation preimage of the coefficient radical. In particular, a single
term is radical exactly when its coefficient is, and a zero coefficient
radical gives the augmentation kernel. See the
[radical guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/Jacobson.md) and
[statements and guides](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#finite-p-groups-and-fixed-vectors).

headlines.title: Given modules and scalar restriction
headlines.text:
**Given modules and scalar restriction.** Over any semiring and monoid,
canonical representations and an additive Hom/intertwiner correspondence
retain the given carriers and coefficient actions. For finite groups of
unit order in the coefficient semiring, coefficient projectivity implies
group-algebra projectivity. The normalized norm is natural for `R[G]`-linear
maps and is the unique `R[G]`-linear retraction onto the fixed vectors' span.
For rings `S`, `A`, a map `φ : S →+* A` surjective modulo a
two-sided ideal `I`, and an `A`-module `V` with
`∃ n, I^n ≤ Module.annihilator A V`, the exact restriction
`Module.compHom V φ` preserves and reflects both chain conditions and
preserves length in `ℕ∞`, including infinity. Semisimplicity is equivalent
to **annihilation by `I` and semisimplicity of that restriction**.
For finite `p`-groups over rings with prime `p = 0`, this gives the canonical
coefficient comparisons: semisimplicity requires coefficient semisimplicity
**and** trivial group action. Fixed vectors detect injectivity of module
maps; coinvariants detect surjectivity, without finite generation.
[Statements and modules](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#given-modules-and-scalar-restriction).

headlines.title: Finiteness of modules
headlines.text:
**Finiteness of modules.** For rings `S`, `A`, compatible scalar towers,
and a two-sided ideal `I`, a Noetherian `A`-module with uniformly nilpotent
`I`-action is finite over `S` whenever `A ⧸ I` is finite over `S`; no
surjective scalar map or nilpotence of `I` itself is needed. Separately,
a simple algebra over a commutative ring admitting a nontrivial compatible
module Noetherian over that base is itself Noetherian, hence finite, over
the base; the base ring need not be Noetherian.
A Noetherian `A`-semimodule also has a greatest `A`-submodule
finite over compatible scalars `S`, preserved by every `A`-linear
endomorphism. For the regular module this is a two-sided ideal. Both
scalar semirings may be noncommutative, and `S` need not be Noetherian.
[Greatest finite submodules](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/GroupRings/RingTheory/Module/ScalarRestriction.lean) ·
[other statements and hypotheses](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#given-modules-and-scalar-restriction).

headlines.title: Subgroup ideals and coset bases
headlines.text:
**Subgroup ideals and coset bases.** Over any ring, a subgroup's left
difference ideal consists of elements whose coefficient sums vanish on
**left cosets** `gH`. Over nontrivial rings these ideals reflect subgroup
membership, inclusion, finite generation and normality via two-sidedness.
Separately, over any semiring, `R[G]` has a **left** `R[H]`-basis indexed by
**right cosets** `H * g`; finite index gives module finiteness.
No normality is required for these coset constructions.
[Statements](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#subgroup-ideals-and-coset-bases) ·
[subgroup guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/SubgroupIdeals.md).

headlines.title: Coefficient and index quotients
headlines.text:
**Coefficient and index quotients.** Over semirings, extension of any left
coefficient ideal is characterized coefficientwise. For any semiring
homomorphism and monoid, coefficient change preserves and reflects zero
kernel powers at each fixed exponent, including zero, without surjectivity.
For `Ring R`,
`Semiring S`, `Group G`, `Monoid M`, and maps `f : R →+* S`, `φ : G →* M`,
the mixed kernel is the sum of the extended coefficient kernel and the
kernel-subgroup difference ideal. For arbitrary maps the quotient is the
composite's range subsemiring; surjective `f` gives `S[MonoidHom.mrange φ]`, and
surjectivity of both gives `S[M]`. Normal-subgroup quotients and unchanged
coefficient kernel/range quotients have full basis and factorization laws.
[Statements and guides](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#coefficient-and-index-quotients).

headlines.title: Commuting scalar actions and central idempotents
headlines.text:
**Commuting scalar actions and central idempotents.** Commuting ring
actions on a module remain commuting after quotienting both rings by
annihilating ideals; two-sidedness is needed for quotient rings, not just
their scalar actions. For any ring `A` and two-sided ideal `I`, the
[first ideal-square quotient](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/GroupRings/RingTheory/Ideal/SquareQuotient.lean)
`I/I²` has commuting left and right `A ⧸ I`-actions. In any ring, an idempotent
central modulo a nilpotent two-sided ideal `I` is central if **both**
off-diagonal corner maps send `I` into `I²`; quotient centrality alone is
insufficient.
[Actions](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#given-modules-and-scalar-restriction) ·
[centrality criterion](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#chain-conditions-and-regularity).

headlines.title: Central summands detected by characters
headlines.text:
**Central summands detected by characters.** For a commutative ring `R`
and an `R`-algebra `A` Artinian on both sides, every `χ : A →ₐ[R] R`
is one on a central idempotent whose principal left ideal is finite over
`R` with its inherited action. Zero and nonreduced base rings are allowed;
the whole algebra need not be finite over `R`.
[Statement and proof strategy](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#central-summands-finite-over-the-base-ring).

headlines.title: Uniform binomial kernels
headlines.text:
**Uniform binomial kernels.** For any monoid homomorphism and any ring,
its monoid-algebra kernel is the left span of equal-image unit-basis
differences. If the source is finitely generated and commutative, one finite
family of index pairs works over **every** coefficient ring. Neither the
target monoid nor the coefficients need commute; no coefficient-Noetherian
hypothesis is needed.
[Statements and modules](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#uniform-binomial-kernels).

headlines.title: Relative module finiteness
headlines.text:
**Relative module finiteness.** For any semiring `R` and homomorphism
`f : M →* N` of arbitrary monoids, `R[N]` is finite as a left `R[M]`-module
for its regular action restricted along `mapDomainRingHom R f` iff there is
a finite set `T` with every `n` expressible as `f m * t`, `t ∈ T`, or `R`
is subsingleton.
The source image is on the **left**; coefficients may be noncommutative,
and neither cancellation nor finite generation is assumed. Monomial
subalgebra inclusions over nontrivial commutative coefficients satisfy the
corresponding finite-cover criterion with their inclusion-induced action.
[Statements and boundaries](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#relative-module-finiteness) ·
[imports and API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/Usage.md#relative-module-finiteness).

headlines.title: Finite type
headlines.text:
**Finite type.** For any commutative semiring `R` and any monoid `M`,
`Algebra.FiniteType R (MonoidAlgebra R M)` is equivalent to
`Monoid.FG M ∨ Subsingleton R`. Nontrivial coefficients give simply finite
generation of `M`; neither commutativity nor cancellation of `M` is needed.
The additive-monoid counterpart uses the same criterion.
[Module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/GroupRings/MonoidAlgebra/FiniteType.lean) ·
[statements and use](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#finite-type).

headlines.title: Finite presentation
headlines.text:
**Finite presentation.** For any commutative ring `R` and finitely generated
commutative monoid `M`, the canonical `R`-algebra `R[M]` is finitely presented.
The additive-monoid version is also an instance. Coefficients need not be
Noetherian, and exponents need not be cancellative or finite.
[Module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/GroupRings/MonoidAlgebra/FinitePresentation.lean) ·
[statements and use](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#finite-presentation).

headlines.title: Chain conditions and regularity
headlines.text:
**Chain conditions and regularity.** For any ring `R` and finitely generated
**commutative** monoid `M`, `R[M]` is left-Noetherian iff `R` is.
For a commutative group `G`, the exact criterion is left-Noetherianity of `R`
and `Subsingleton R ∨ Group.FG G`. A finite-index finitely generated
commutative subgroup gives the coefficient-ring criterion even when the
ambient group is noncommutative and the subgroup is not normal. For a
cancellative monoid over any semiring, a **nonzero** left ideal finite over
the coefficients forces the monoid to be finite. Additive right-compatible
coefficient retractions give left-Artinian descent without multiplicativity.
Such a retraction exists for every homomorphism from a division ring to a
nontrivial semiring, without centrality or finite-dimensionality assumptions.
Left-Noetherianity descends to embedded group algebras over any semiring;
finite-index subgroup algebras over rings share it with the whole algebra.
Over nontrivial rings it forces every subgroup to be finitely generated,
without a general converse. The infinite cyclic and finite-index cyclic
criteria reduce to the coefficient ring; import
`GroupRings.MonoidAlgebra.CyclicNoetherian` directly for these.
Over any ring, infinite-order elements of cancellative monoids give regular
monic basis differences, forcing torsion in left-Artinian monoid algebras
with nontrivial coefficients. For any ring `R` and either a left-cancellative
or a right-cancellative monoid `G`,
[`MonoidAlgebra.isArtinianRing_iff_of_isLeftCancelMul` and
`MonoidAlgebra.isArtinianRing_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/GroupRings/MonoidAlgebra/Artinian.lean)
give that `R[G]` is left-Artinian iff `R` is left-Artinian and
`Subsingleton R ∨ Finite G`. The corresponding `finite_of_isArtinianRing`
theorems give monoid finiteness directly over any nontrivial ring,
specializing to the classical group criterion.
Locally, over a nontrivial **semiring** and any monoid, left Artinianity
makes every right-regular index a unit; over a nontrivial **ring**, it also
makes every left-regular index a unit, without global cancellation.
The global criteria require **ring** coefficients. All these conditions
use the original left regular action.
The zero ring is allowed in the criterion, the
universes are independent, and no commutativity or right-Artinian hypothesis
is imposed.
Separately, `LaurentPolynomial R` is left-Artinian iff `R` is subsingleton,
even for noncommutative or zero rings.
[Statements and modules](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#chain-conditions-and-regularity).

headlines.title: Laurent coordinates
headlines.text:
**Laurent coordinates.** Supplied coordinates `G ≃+ (σ →₀ ℤ)` identify an
additive commutative group's algebra over a commutative semiring with
`MvLaurentPolynomial σ A`. Free abelian groups have canonical coordinates,
with arbitrary, empty or infinite variable types.
[Statements and module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#laurent-coordinates).

headlines.title: Characters and right convolution
headlines.text:
**Characters and right convolution.** Character evaluations on an additive
commutative group `G` are linearly independent over any field `K`, even for
infinite groups without enough roots. For finite `G`, enough roots of unity
of exponent `Monoid.exponent (Multiplicative G)` give a character basis;
with `[Fintype G]` they give diagonalization and rank for right convolution,
whose entry is `f (-sigma + tau)` and eigenvalue is `∑ x, f x * psi x` with
**positive** sign. The eigenvector law needs no enough-roots assumption.
[Statements](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/HeadlineResults.md#characters-and-right-convolution) ·
[Fourier guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-rings/blob/8e90e6563300656410a098a0fea83332930218b5/docs/FiniteAbelianRightConvolution.md).

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.ker_mapRingHom_pow_eq_bot_iff
main_results.note: For any homomorphism between independently universed semirings and any monoid, the coefficient-map kernel has zero n-th power iff the coefficient kernel does, at the same n including zero; no commutativity, nontriviality, surjectivity or finiteness.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.eq_iff_forall_mul_coeff_eq_right
main_results.note: For any semiring and group in independent universes, equality is equivalent to equality at one fixed arbitrary coefficient in every right product. Zero and noncommutative coefficients and infinite groups are allowed.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.eq_iff_forall_mul_coeff_eq_left
main_results.note: The separate criterion for every left product, preserving coefficient multiplication order.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.eq_zero_iff_forall_mul_coeff_eq_zero_right
main_results.note: Vanishing of one fixed coefficient in every right product detects the zero element over any semiring.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.eq_zero_iff_forall_mul_coeff_eq_zero_left
main_results.note: The corresponding zero characterization for all left products; index one specializes to identity-coefficient separation without an extra declaration.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.mem_center_iff
main_results.note: For arbitrary semirings and groups in independent universes, centrality is equivalent to central coefficients and conjugation invariance, including zero and noncommutative coefficients.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.coeff_mem_center
main_results.note: Every coefficient of a central monoid-algebra element is central, for any semiring and monoid; no group assumption is needed.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.coeff_conj_of_mem_center
main_results.note: Coefficients of central group-algebra elements are invariant under conjugation.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.finite_conjAct_orbit_of_coeff_ne_zero
main_results.note: A nonzero coefficient of a central element forces that label's canonical conjugation orbit to be finite, not the group to be finite or the label central.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.coeff_eq_zero_of_not_finite_conjAct_orbit
main_results.note: Every coefficient of a central group-algebra element vanishes on an infinite conjugation orbit.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.mem_center_iff_of_subsingleton
main_results.note: For a one-element group, centrality reduces to centrality of the identity coefficient, without commutativity or nontriviality of coefficients.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.mem_center_iff_coeff_conj
main_results.note: For commutative semiring coefficients, centrality is equivalent to conjugation invariance alone.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.matrixRingEquiv
main_results.note: Canonical ring equivalence between a monoid algebra of finite square matrices and matrices of monoid-algebra entries, with forward/inverse coefficient and single-term laws over arbitrary semirings and monoids, including empty matrix indices.

main_results.name: Ideal.isNoetherian_iff_of_pow_le_annihilator
main_results.note: For arbitrary rings, quotient-surjective scalar restriction and a uniformly nilpotent two-sided ideal action preserve and reflect Noetherianity; exact Module.compHom action and independent universes.

main_results.name: Ideal.isArtinian_iff_of_pow_le_annihilator
main_results.note: The separate Artinian equivalence under the same hypotheses, without finite generation or finite length.

main_results.name: Ideal.length_eq_of_pow_le_annihilator
main_results.note: Equality of canonical composition lengths in ENat, including infinity, under the same hypotheses. Nilpotent-ideal corollaries require no module-specific bound.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isNoetherian_iff_of_isPGroup
main_results.note: Every module of a finite p-group algebra over any ring with prime p=0 is Noetherian iff its canonical coefficient restriction is.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isArtinian_iff_of_isPGroup
main_results.note: The corresponding separate Artinian equivalence for any given module, including noncommutative and zero coefficients.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.length_eq_of_isPGroup
main_results.note: Canonical ring-relative length over R[G] equals that under moduleCoefficientModule, including infinite length; no field-dimension claim.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.injective_iff_fixedVectorMap
main_results.note: Every map of unital modules over any finite p-group algebra with prime p=0 in R is injective iff its canonical fixed-vector map is injective; independent universes, no finite generation, commutativity or nontriviality premise.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.surjective_iff_coinvariantMap
main_results.note: Surjectivity iff surjectivity on the original augmentation-ideal-action quotients, with canonical coefficient actions and the same arbitrary-ring finite-p-group hypotheses.

main_results.name: LinearMap.injective_iff_annihilatorSubmoduleMap
main_results.note: A nilpotent two-sided ideal detects genuine injectivity on common annihilators over any semiring acting on additive groups.

main_results.name: LinearMap.surjective_iff_mapQ_smul_top
main_results.note: The usual quotient-induced map modulo any nilpotent left ideal detects surjectivity over any ring, without finite generation.

main_results.name: Submodule.eq_bot_of_isNilpotent_of_smul_eq_self
main_results.note: A submodule equal to its product by a nilpotent left ideal is zero, over any semiring and semimodule.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isSimpleModule_iff_of_isPGroup
main_results.note: For any Ring R, finite p-group G and unital module V with prime p=0 in R, simplicity over R[G] iff simplicity under the canonical coefficient restriction; independent universes and no extra module hypotheses.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.smul_eq_augmentation_smul_of_isSimpleModule_of_isPGroup
main_results.note: Every scalar acts on every vector of a simple finite-p-group-algebra module through augmentation and the same coefficient embedding.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.smul_eq_augmentation_smul_iff
main_results.note: For arbitrary semirings, monoids and semimodules, augmentation action iff every canonical monoid symbol fixes every vector.

main_results.name: Ideal.exists_ne_zero_le_torsionOf_of_pow_le_annihilator
main_results.note: Uniformly nilpotent action of an ordinary left ideal on a nontrivial semimodule over any semiring yields a nonzero common annihilated vector.

main_results.name: Ideal.annihilatorSubmodule
main_results.note: Common-annihilator submodule for two-sided ideals over semirings, with the largest-submodule universal property and commutative set-torsion agreement.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.ker_augmentation_le_torsionOf_iff
main_results.note: For arbitrary rings, monoids and vectors of unital modules, augmentation-kernel annihilation iff canonical-symbol fixedness.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.exists_ne_zero_fixed_of_isPGroup
main_results.note: Any nontrivial unital module of a finite p-group algebra over any possibly noncommutative ring with prime p=0 has a nonzero canonical fixed vector, with no module finiteness hypothesis.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.augmentation_pow_card_eq_bot
main_results.note: For a finite p-group over any possibly noncommutative ring with prime p=0, the canonical augmentation kernel has zero Nat.card G-th power, including the zero coefficient ring.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.augmentation_list_prod_eq_zero
main_results.note: Every ordered mixed product of Nat.card G augmentation elements vanishes under the same all-ring finite-p-group hypotheses.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isNilpotent_augmentation_iff_isPGroup
main_results.note: For finite groups over nontrivial rings with prime p=0, canonical ideal nilpotence is equivalent to IsPGroup p G.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isNilpotent_of_augmentation_eq_zero
main_results.note: For any Ring R, prime p with (p : R) = 0, and Group G with IsPGroup p G and finite subgroup closure of every finite subset, each augmentation-zero element is nilpotent; no uniform exponent or zero power of the whole kernel is asserted. The coefficient and group universes are independent.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.jacobson_eq_comap_augmentation
main_results.note: For any possibly noncommutative or zero Ring R, prime p with (p : R) = 0, and Group G with IsPGroup p G and finite subgroup closure of every finite subset, Ring.jacobson R[G] is the augmentation preimage of Ring.jacobson R; independent coefficient and group universes, with no uniform nilpotence assumption.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.mem_jacobson_iff_augmentation_mem
main_results.note: Under the same locally finite p-group hypotheses, an element lies in the Jacobson radical exactly when its coefficient sum lies in the coefficient radical.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.single_mem_jacobson_iff
main_results.note: Under the same hypotheses, single g r lies in the radical exactly when r does; g=1 gives canonical coefficient inclusion.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.jacobson_eq_ker_augmentation_of_jacobson_eq_bot
main_results.note: Under the same hypotheses and Ring.jacobson R = bottom, the group-algebra Jacobson radical is the canonical augmentation kernel.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.ker_mapDomainRingHom_mk'_zpowers
main_results.note: For a normal cyclic subgroup, the quotient index-map kernel is the left ideal generated by the single generator difference, over any ring.

main_results.name: Ideal.map_pow_le
main_results.note: Semiring homomorphisms extend left-ideal powers into powers of the extended ideal; equality and target commutativity are not assumed.

main_results.name: Ideal.pow_mul
main_results.note: Iteration of left-ideal powers multiplies degrees over any semiring, including zero degrees, without two-sidedness.

main_results.name: Ideal.pow_le_iff_forall_list_prod_mem
main_results.note: Universal property of powers of arbitrary left ideals over semirings via ordered mixed lists, including length zero; no two-sidedness or nontriviality.

main_results.name: Ideal.pow_eq_bot_iff_forall_list_prod_eq_zero
main_results.note: The n-th power vanishes exactly when every ordered length-n mixed product vanishes, including n=0.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.forall_pow_eq_one_of_augmentation_pow_eq_bot
main_results.note: Over a nontrivial ring with prime p=0, a zero n-th augmentation power forces every p^k at least n to be a common group exponent.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.exists_pow_eq_one_of_isNilpotent_augmentation
main_results.note: Nilpotence forces one common p-power exponent for an arbitrary group, not only pointwise p-power torsion.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.exists_pow_eq_one_of_augmentation_products_eq_zero
main_results.note: Uniform mixed-product nilpotence has the same common-exponent consequence without a finite-group assumption.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isPGroup_of_isNilpotent_augmentation
main_results.note: The common exponent gives IsPGroup p G as a corollary for nontrivial rings with prime p=0.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.mem_map_singleOneRingHom_iff
main_results.note: For every left ideal over any semiring and any monoid, extension by constants is equivalent to membership of every coefficient.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.ker_mapRingHom
main_results.note: The kernel of coefficient change is the extension of the coefficient kernel, without commutativity, nontriviality, additive inverses or surjectivity.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.quotientCoeffKerEquiv
main_results.note: For Ring R, Semiring S and surjective f, the coefficient-kernel quotient is S[M], characterized on all classes and every basis coefficient.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.ker_mapDomainRingHom_comp_mapRingHom
main_results.note: For Ring R, Semiring S, Group G and Monoid M, the simultaneous kernel is the sum of the subgroup-difference ideal and extended coefficient kernel, with no surjectivity assumptions.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.quotientMixedKerEquivMrange
main_results.note: Surjective coefficients identify the mixed quotient with the monoid algebra of the index range; simultaneous surjectivity also gives the full target. Arbitrary maps instead have the composite range subsemiring as quotient target.

main_results.name: Polynomial.map_ker_toMultiplicative_toFinsuppIso
main_results.note: The stock polynomial equivalence followed by the additive-to-multiplicative index equivalence transports coefficient kernels; companion laws preserve arbitrary coefficient ideals, polynomials and constants.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isNoetherianRing_multiplicative_int_iff
main_results.note: For every ring, including noncommutative and zero rings, the infinite cyclic group algebra is left-Noetherian iff its coefficient ring is; uses Laurent ascent from multivariate-polynomials and Mathlib ring transport.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isNoetherianRing_iff_of_mulEquiv_int
main_results.note: A supplied group equivalence with Multiplicative Int transports the coefficient criterion, with independent coefficient and group universes and no scalar or carrier replacement.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isNoetherianRing_iff_of_finiteIndex_mulEquiv_int
main_results.note: For a finite-index subgroup supplied with an equivalence to the infinite cyclic group, left-Noetherianity of the whole group algebra is equivalent to that of the arbitrary coefficient ring; no normality is needed.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isNoetherianRing_multiplicative_int_prod_iff
main_results.note: Products of the infinite cyclic group with any finite group satisfy the same coefficient-ring criterion, using the second projection kernel and its first-coordinate group equivalence.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isNoetherianRing_of_fg
main_results.note: A finitely generated commutative monoid algebra over an arbitrary left-Noetherian ring is left-Noetherian, in independent universes. The exponent monoid need not be finite and coefficients need not commute. Uses finite-coordinate ascent from multivariate-polynomials and a surjective exponent presentation with coefficient-preserving ring transport.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isNoetherianRing_of_injective
main_results.note: Over any semiring, an injective group-to-monoid homomorphism descends regular-left Noetherianity of monoid algebras, in three independent universes.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isNoetherianRing_subgroup
main_results.note: Every subgroup algebra of a left-Noetherian group algebra is left-Noetherian, without finite index or normality.

main_results.name: RingHom.isNoetherianRing_of_additive_retraction
main_results.note: An additive retraction E of a semiring hom f, satisfying E(b*f(a)) = E(b)*a, descends left Noetherianity via ideal extension-contraction.

main_results.name: RingHom.comap_map_eq_of_additive_retraction
main_results.note: Extension followed by contraction fixes every left ideal under an additive right retraction; comap_map_eq_of_leftInverse supplies the RingHom specialization.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.comapDomain_mul_mapDomain
main_results.note: Coefficient pullback commutes with right multiplication by a group image in an arbitrary target monoid; coefficients retain their original order.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.subgroup_fg_of_isNoetherianRing
main_results.note: Every subgroup of a group with left-Noetherian group algebra over a nontrivial possibly noncommutative ring is finitely generated; scalar ring is R[G], not R.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.augmentation_surjective
main_results.note: Surjectivity over any semiring and monoid, with independent universes, allowing generic stock Noetherianity transport to the coefficient semiring.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.ker_mapDomainRingHom_mk'
main_results.note: For arbitrary ring coefficients, the kernel of the normal-quotient index map is the independently specified left span of the subgroup differences.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.quotientSpanSubgroupEquiv
main_results.note: The first-isomorphism ring equivalence has all-element and full single g r characteristic formulas and is uniquely characterized by its values on quotient classes.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.existsUnique_comp_mapDomainRingHom_mk'_iff
main_results.note: An arbitrary unital ring homomorphism into any semiring factors uniquely through the quotient index map exactly when every subgroup basis unit maps to one; the three universes are independent.

main_results.name: AddMonoidAlgebra.mem_ideal_of_mapDomain_eq_zero
main_results.note: All-coefficient basis normalization puts mapped-zero elements in a left ideal, over any ring and additive source monoid with an arbitrary target index type.

main_results.name: AddMonoidAlgebra.ker_mapDomainRingHom_le
main_results.note: The normalization principle contains an additive-monoid map kernel in the specified left ideal; no surjectivity or section law is required.

main_results.name: AddMonoidAlgebra.ideal_eq_ker_mapDomainRingHom
main_results.note: All-coefficient normalization plus the separate ideal-to-kernel containment gives kernel equality.

main_results.name: AddMonoidAlgebra.mem_ideal_iff_mapDomain_eq_zero
main_results.note: Membership in a normalized left ideal is equivalent to vanishing under the additive monomial map once the ideal is contained in the kernel.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.ker_mapDomainRingHom_eq_span_fiber
main_results.note: For arbitrary monoids and any ring, the induced-map kernel is the ordinary left span of all equal-image unit-basis differences, in independent universes.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.uniform_fiber_span_of_integer_kernel_fg
main_results.note: For arbitrary source and target monoids, finite generation of the integer kernel supplies one finite same-fiber pair set generating every ring-coefficient kernel as a left ideal.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.uniform_fiber_span_of_fg
main_results.note: An FG commutative source and arbitrary monoid target admit one finite pair set before quantification over every independently universed ring; no coefficient-Noetherian or target-generation assumption.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.ker_mapDomainRingHom
main_results.note: For any group-to-monoid homomorphism and any ring, its algebra pushforward kernel is the independently generated left subgroup relation ideal; no surjectivity, coefficient nontriviality or target group assumption is needed.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.quotientSpanKerEquivMrange
main_results.note: The canonical quotient is ring-equivalent to the monoid algebra of the stock range submonoid, with all-class and full basis-coefficient formulas and uniqueness.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.quotientSpanKerEquivOfSurjective
main_results.note: For a surjective group-to-monoid map the range equivalence specializes to the whole target algebra, with characteristic formulas and uniqueness.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.existsUnique_comp_mapDomainRingHom_mrangeRestrict_iff
main_results.note: A homomorphism into any semiring factors uniquely through the range pushforward exactly when every kernel basis unit maps to one; all four universes are independent.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.existsUnique_comp_mapDomainRingHom_of_surjective_iff
main_results.note: Only under index surjectivity is the same unique factorization asserted through the whole target monoid algebra.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.cosetSum
main_results.note: Over any semiring and group, sum coefficients on left cosets into the existing finitely supported coefficient module; cosetSum_single and cosetSum_apply give its basis and finite-support laws.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.mem_span_subgroup_iff
main_results.note: Over any ring, membership in the ordinary left span of subgroup differences iff the coset sum is zero; no normality or nontriviality assumption.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.single_sub_one_mem_span_subgroup_iff
main_results.note: Over a nontrivial ring, a basis difference belongs to the subgroup left ideal iff its index is in the subgroup.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.span_subgroup_le_iff
main_results.note: Over a nontrivial ring, inclusion of subgroup left ideals iff inclusion of subgroups. Forward monotonicity needs no nontriviality and follows from span_mono.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.span_subgroup_isTwoSided
main_results.note: Normality implies two-sidedness over any possibly trivial or noncommutative ring.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.span_subgroup_isTwoSided_iff
main_results.note: Over a nontrivial ring, two-sidedness of the subgroup left ideal iff the subgroup is normal.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.span_subgroup_fg_of_fg
main_results.note: For any Ring R and Group G in independent universes, H.FG implies FG of the ordinary left ideal spanned by single h 1 - 1; no normality or nontriviality is required.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.span_subgroup_fg_iff
main_results.note: Over a nontrivial Ring R, the subgroup left ideal is FG iff H is FG, with scalars R[G], not R.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.ker_augmentation_fg
main_results.note: For a Group.FG group over any Ring R, including the zero ring, the augmentation kernel is a finitely generated left ideal.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.ker_augmentation_fg_iff
main_results.note: Over a nontrivial Ring R, the augmentation kernel is FG as a left ideal iff Group.FG G.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isUnit_coeff_of_single
main_results.note: Under Semiring R and Monoid M, a unit single m r has unit coefficient r, without a nontriviality assumption.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isLocalHom_of
main_results.note: Under Semiring R, Nontrivial R and Monoid M, the basis embedding of R M reflects units.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.isUnit_single_iff
main_results.note: Under Semiring R, Nontrivial R and Monoid M, IsUnit (single m r) iff IsUnit r and IsUnit m. No commutativity, cancellation, group, domain or finiteness hypothesis is required.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.augmentation
main_results.note: Coefficient-sum ring homomorphism under Semiring R and Monoid M, in independent universes.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.augmentation_apply
main_results.note: The augmentation of x is x.coeff.sum (fun _ r => r).

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.augmentation_single
main_results.note: A single basis term augments to its coefficient.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.ker_augmentation
main_results.note: Under Ring R and Monoid M, the kernel is Ideal.span of the range of single m 1 - 1, a left ideal even for noncommutative R.

main_results.name: Ideal.sub_one_mem_of_mem_submonoid_closure
main_results.note: For Ring A, Monoid M, a left ideal I and u : M →* A, membership of u s - 1 in I propagates from S to Submonoid.closure S.

main_results.name: Ideal.sub_one_mem_of_mem_subgroup_closure
main_results.note: The group-domain companion uses ordinary Subgroup.closure, with no group structure on A or two-sidedness of I.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.ker_augmentation_eq_span_of_submonoid_closure_eq_top
main_results.note: Under Ring R and Monoid M, Submonoid.closure S = top implies the augmentation kernel is the left span of single s 1 - 1 for s in S.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.ker_augmentation_eq_span_of_subgroup_closure_eq_top
main_results.note: For Group G, ordinary subgroup generation suffices for the same left-span formula; no normal closure is used.

main_results.name: Finsupp.kerLsumEquiv
main_results.note: For Semiring S, AddCommGroup V, Module S V and b : T, the kernel of lsum ℕ (fun _ => LinearMap.id) is S-linearly equivalent to {t : T // t ≠ b} →₀ V by restriction. The inverse extends and subtracts single b (sum g).

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.sumCoords_basis_apply
main_results.note: Under Semiring R and Monoid M, the coordinate sum in the monoid-algebra basis equals augmentation pointwise.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.ker_augmentation_restrictScalars
main_results.note: Under Semiring R and Monoid M, the existing kernel restricted to R is the kernel of the linear coefficient sum composed with coeffLinearEquiv.

main_results.name: MonoidAlgebra.augmentationKerBasis
main_results.note: Under Ring R and Monoid M, a basis of the augmentation kernel restricted to left coefficient scalars R, indexed by {m : M // m ≠ 1}; vector and repr-coordinate laws are coe_augmentationKerBasis and augmentationKerBasis_repr_apply. No commutativity or nontriviality hypothesis.

main_results.name: MvLaurentPolynomial
main_results.note: Abbreviation for AddMonoidAlgebra A (σ →₀ ℤ), under Semiring A, including noncommutative coefficients.

main_results.name: AddEquiv.monoidAlgebraMultiplicativeEquivMvLaurentPolynomial
main_results.note: Under CommSemiring A and AddCommGroup G, supplied e : G ≃+ (σ →₀ ℤ) induces the A-algebra equivalence; coefficient/group/index universes are independent.

main_results.name: AddEquiv.monoidAlgebraMultiplicativeEquivMvLaurentPolynomial_single
main_results.note: Forward law: single (ofAdd g) a maps to the Laurent basis term single (e g) a.

main_results.name: AddEquiv.monoidAlgebraMultiplicativeEquivMvLaurentPolynomial_symm_single
main_results.note: Inverse law: single m a maps to single (ofAdd (e.symm m)) a.

main_results.name: FreeAbelianGroup.monoidAlgebraEquivMvLaurentPolynomial
main_results.note: Canonical specialization through FreeAbelianGroup.equivFinsupp, under CommSemiring A and arbitrary index type.

main_results.name: FreeAbelianGroup.monoidAlgebraEquivMvLaurentPolynomial_single
main_results.note: Forward canonical basis law uses the exponent vector equivFinsupp sigma g.

main_results.name: FreeAbelianGroup.monoidAlgebraEquivMvLaurentPolynomial_symm_single
main_results.note: Inverse canonical basis law uses (equivFinsupp sigma).symm m.

main_results.name: FreeAbelianGroup.monoidAlgebraEquivMvLaurentPolynomial_generator
main_results.note: The free generator of i maps to exponent Finsupp.single i 1, with arbitrary coefficient a.

main_results.name: AddChar.linearIndependent_field
main_results.note: Dedekind independence of evaluations AddChar G K into G → K over a field, without finiteness or enough-roots assumptions.

main_results.name: AddChar.finite_of_field
main_results.note: A finite additive abelian group has finitely many field-valued characters, without an enough-roots assumption.

main_results.name: AddChar.natCard_eq_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity
main_results.note: The dual and G have the same Nat.card given finiteness and enough roots of unity of the group exponent.

main_results.name: AddChar.basisOfEnoughRootsOfUnity
